title: Reidemeister moves between closed braids factor through Markov moves
statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $B$ and $C$ be closed braid diagrams
representing the same oriented link. Then $B$ can be transformed into $C$ by a
sequence of braid isotopies of closed braid diagrams, Markov stabilizations and
destabilizations, and their inverses; equivalently, the braids read from $B$
and $C$ are Markov equivalent.
strategy: First use the generating and height-zero suppliers to isolate reducing sequences with height-zero endpoints. Eliminate every peak at the current maximum height: the peak-lowering supplier gives finitely many compatible valleys and irreducible four-band peaks, and the four-band supplier joins the latter's descending reductions at height zero. None of these replacements reintroduces the removed height; removing the finitely many original maxima lowers the whole maximum. Induct on the natural-number height. The four-band computation and the recursive height-zero proof obligations remain escalated; this corrected termination argument does not certify them.

references.title: Traczyk, A new proof of Markov's braid theorem, Banach Center Publications 42 (1998), 409-419
Birman and Brendle, Braids: A Survey, Handbook of Knot Theory chapter, author manuscript; section 2 (printed pp. 12-26) and Figures 3-12
